immensee: Theodor Storm's tender German novella follows Reinhard, who returns to the lake of his childhood and remembers Elisabeth, the love he lost through hesitation. Memory, music, and the passage of time weave through prose of great delicacy. A small masterpiece of European literature, beloved for its gentle melancholy.
story-hour-readers-book-three: Ida Coe's third Story Hour Reader gathers stories, poems, and fables chosen to build young readers' skills and character. Short selections with sturdy morals made it a classroom favorite of its era. A charming example of how American schools once taught children to read — and to be good.
jack-harkaway-and-his-son-s-escape-from-: Bracebridge Hemyng's immortal Jack Harkaway — schoolboy hero turned adventurer — escapes the brigands of Greece with his son. The penny-dreadful king at his most thrilling. Pure Victorian excitement. Daggers, dungeons, and daring mark every chapter of this breathless tale. Hemyng's hero never knew the meaning of fear.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acanthus-titu: A 1913 entry on Acanthus as a titular see — the vanished bishopric kept alive in name. The old city's faith outlived its walls. A brief note for students of the hierarchy. The Church forgets no see. Its bishops now serve the wider Church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-augus: This 1913 reference article on Antoine-Augustin Touttée — a Benedictine editor of note. Michael Ott records his works. The entry preserves his modest fame. His pen served the Maurist press. A monk among the editors. His Cyril edition graced the press.
